transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-29 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (AE), Maya Patel (SE) - Redwood; Liam O'Connor, Sana Rahman, Ethan Park - ACME Search

Summary: Short demo of hosted embeddings + reranking. Focus on relevance workflow, integration patterns, security and pilot next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Kim from Redwood, and with me is Maya Patel, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Liam: Good, thanks. Liam O'Connor here. Excited to see how you handle embeddings + rerank.
[00:12] Sana: Hi, Sana. We run search across product catalogs and support docs, so relevance is the big pain point.
[00:18] Maya: Great, that's exactly what we planned to walk through. We'll show the hosted embeddings endpoint, the rerank API pattern, and then a quick tour of the console Optimize suggestions.
[00:28] Jordan: Quick agenda: demo the API calls, show a live rerank example with a sample query and results, discuss latency/cost tradeoffs, security and next steps for a pilot.
[00:36] Ethan: Sounds good. Our main constraint: p95 latency under 200ms for queries that hit the reranker, and we need strong data controls.
[00:44] Maya: Understood. We'll show typical latencies for hosted and options if you need dedicated capacity.

[02:05] Maya: Ok first, embeddings. We have a hosted embeddings endpoint that returns 1024-d vectors by default for the model we onboarded. Example payload... (reads code) POST /v1/embeddings body: {"input": "product description"} returns vector and id.
[02:29] Sana: Do you persist embeddings automatically? We don't want customer PII stored.
[02:35] Maya: By default in hosted we keep embeddings for caching and performance but you can opt out — data retention flags or have them not stored, or use private deployment. For enterprise we also support BYOK KMS and configurable retention windows.
[02:52] Liam: What's default TTL?
[02:55] Maya: Default is 30 days for ephemeral caching; for longer you'd configure in Console or opt into Dedicated/Private. I'll share the exact policy doc.

[05:10] Jordan: Moving to rerank. Two typical patterns: 1) vector search + client-side rescoring where you fetch top-K from your vector DB and call our rerank endpoint to reorder — low bandwidth, serverless; 2) server-side rerank where you send candidate docs and query and we return top result set. We'll demo pattern 1.
[05:36] Maya: Live demo: I have a sample dataset loaded in Composer and a simple vector DB (we're simulating Pinecone here). Query is "fast charge battery not holding". I'll run search, then call /v1/rerank with candidates + original query.
[05:54] [05:55] (keyboard sounds)
[06:22] Maya: Ok results returned. Before rerank the vector DB's top 5 had a couple of off-topic product pages. With reranker top-3 are now on-target FAQ + troubleshooting guide.
[06:36] Sana: Nice. How do you handle hallucination in the reranker — sometimes LLMs prefer verbose pages that look good but are wrong.
[06:44] Maya: Good point. We combine lexical features + embedding similarity and you can include signals like click-through, recency as features. We also have a safety pass and you can pin exact-match rules. The reranker model is tuned for relevance not generation.

[09:05] Ethan: Latency numbers? If we do fetch top-K (K=10) then call rerank, what's p95?
[09:12] Maya: For hosted we typically see ~40-120ms for the rerank call depending on model size and payload (10 candidates). For your 200ms p95 target we'd be comfortable but it depends on network + vector DB time. If you need sub-100ms consistently we can talk Dedicated and co-locating the vector DB in the same region.
[09:33] Liam: Any batching or concurrency tips to reduce cost?
[09:37] Jordan: Yes, Optimize suggestions in the Console will recommend batching thresholds, candidate K tuning, and lower-cost model variants for bulk rerank jobs.

[12:10] Maya: I'm going to show the Console now — quick screen share — Dashboard shows per-route latency and token breakdown, and an Optimize tab that suggests reducing K from 20 to 8 for this workload, which drops cost ~35% with minimal loss in NDCG in our test.
[12:30] [12:31] (screen share)
[12:45] Maya: Also showing a rollout: you can A/B a reranker model — current production, canary 5%, monitor click-through and rollback automatically.
[13:02] Sana: That's helpful — we want to test impact on CTR before full rollout.

[15:00] Jordan: Security checklist — we support SOC 2, will share certs; SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC for team members, audit logs, and optional VPC peering for private flows. You can BYOK via KMS/HSM.
[15:18] Liam: Good, can we get a copy of the SOC2 and the detailed data flow diagram?
[15:22] Jordan: Yes I'll attach the pack. Maya will share the network diagrams.

[18:40] Maya: Back to integration: rerank request format is fairly compact — query, list of candidate ids + optional metadata features. We support sending candidate text if you prefer server-side scoring. There's also a streaming response option but typically for rerank the synchronous call is simpler.
[19:05] Ethan: If we want to keep vector DB on-prem, can we still use hosted reranker?
[19:10] Maya: Yes — common pattern is fetch top-K from your on-prem vector DB and call hosted reranker (we recommend TLS and a private peering link if you want lower latency). If you need the reranker on-prem we can discuss Private deployment.

[22:00] Liam: How about model versioning — if you retrain an internal reranker model, how do we pin?
[22:06] Maya: You can pin model versions per route in the Console and create rollout policies. We also support labels and canarying like I showed.

[26:30] Sana: One thing — our support docs have lots of short fragments. Embedding quality for short docs can vary. Do you recommend chunking?
[26:40] Maya: Yes chunking with overlap and using semantic-aware chunk sizes works best. Optimize will suggest chunk sizes after analyzing a sample. We'll include our chunker script in the benchmark package.

[30:05] Jordan: Cost note — embeddings are billed per vector generation; rerank calls billed by compute tier and candidate volume. We provided a rough estimate in the deck but we'll send a tailored pilot cost based on your traffic profile.

[32:50] Ethan: Competitors — we've seen Pinecone + a reranker service, and also considering using Elastic with learned reranking. How do you compare?
[32:58] Jordan: Pinecone is a strong vector DB; our value is the unified runtime and reranker + optimize tooling. Elastic is good for lexical matching; Redwood focuses on production inference — telemetry, rollouts, and cost controls.

[36:15] Maya: Quick note about accuracy monitoring — Console can track evaluation metrics on a test set overtime; if quality regresses we can auto alert and trigger rollback.

[39:40] Sana: For the pilot, what telemetry do we get? Click-through, latency, per-route cost?
[39:45] Jordan: Yes, per-route tokens, cost estimate, latency percentiles, and sample request traces. We can also hook logs to your SIEM via audit log export.

[42:00] Liam: Anything we need from our side to start a pilot?
[42:05] Maya: Sample dataset (a few thousand queries + ground truth) and traffic profile, plus an API key and optional SSO admin. We'll send a benchmark harness that you can run against your dev vector DB.

[45:20] Jordan: Let's recap next steps: we'll send pricing and pilot plan, Maya will share benchmark script and sample dataset, and ACME will provide traffic profile and SSO contact. Aim to kick off week of 2026-11-08.
[45:40] Liam: Works for us.
[46:05] Sana: One last question: can rerank output be deterministic across calls? We need consistent ordering for reproducible tests.
[46:15] Maya: Yes you can set a deterministic seed and disable stochastic sampling; reranker is deterministic by default for scoring tasks unless you enable sampling. I'll add notes in the docs.

[49:00] Jordan: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the deck and docs.
[49:10] Ethan: Thanks, that was helpful.
[49:12] Liam: Thanks all.

[52:00] (call ends)

Notes: Imperfect transcription: occasional overlap and minor mis-hear of technical acronyms (e.g., KV cache transcribed as K-V cash, Pinecone sometimes shown as "pine cone"). References shared: demo deck link (internal), benchmark harness (link), SOC2 pack (link).

Action recap in chat: Jordan to send pricing and security pack, Maya to share benchmark script and chunker examples, ACME to provide traffic profile and SSO admin contact.
